A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Reti-Diff, and their main text, equations, tables and figures are readable and matchable. However, v1 refers to supplementary material and v2 to an appendix for the illumination-prior derivation; neither supplied PDF contains that material. This specifically limits the theory comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-enhancement experiments, component ablations, downstream detection and segmentation results, and a 29-participant user study.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds real-world dataset evaluations, computational-efficiency measurements, further ablations and failure examples.

M1.justification: The documented RPE, RLDM, RGformer, RG-MCA, DFA, auxiliary decoder, two-phase training and inference procedures remain unchanged. The loss weights introduced explicitly in Equations (8) and (14) all equal one, preserving v1's objectives.

E1.justification: v2 adds DICM, LIME, MEF, NPE and VV evaluations on real-world images without paired ground truth (Section 4.2, Table 4). These introduce an unseen-degradation testing scenario beyond the retained enhancement and downstream datasets. Extending ablations to the already-used LOL-v2-real dataset is not additional dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 replaces DeepLPF and DBRN with PyDiff and GSAD. The new real-world comparison introduces additional comparators including KinD++, DCC-Net, UHDFor, PairLIE and GDP. v2 also adds a Baseline row to each downstream comparison and KinD to the user study, substantially expanding the comparison evidence.

E3.justification: v2 introduces evaluation of LOL-v2-synthetic-pretrained models on five unpaired real-world datasets using PI and NIQE, plus efficiency evaluation using parameters, MACs and FPS. The original training budgets, architecture settings and user-study design remain stable. Newly explicit per-method downstream retraining does not establish that the earlier protocol changed.

E4.justification: v2 extends component ablations and RLDM transfer analyses to LOL-v2-real, adds separate reflectance-only and illumination-only prior controls (Tables 6–7), and tests replacing DiffIR's LDM with RLDM (Section 5). Figure 10 adds concrete failure cases. The original component-removal and diffusion-iteration analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and user-study averages without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The study still involves 29 participants. Additional result entries do not change the uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original enhancement scores remain unchanged, but v2 adds real-world, efficiency and ablation results and revises downstream scores. ExDark mean AP is reported as 78.2 versus Retformer's 66.1 in v1 Table 7, and 75.8 versus 72.5 in v2 Table 9. These are revised reports, not established same-setting performance changes. Semantic-segmentation comparator scores also change; Reti-Diff's 61.78 to 61.8 is only rounding.

T1.justification: The available Retinex and diffusion equations remain mathematically equivalent; the explicitly introduced unit loss weights do not change them. However, both versions refer the illumination-prior derivation to supplementary material absent from the supplied PDFs, preventing a complete judgment about derivation changes.

C1.justification: Both retain the same central contributions: the claimed first latent-diffusion solution for illumination degradation restoration, Retinex priors generated by RLDM, RGformer-based restoration, and superiority across three enhancement tasks and downstream applications. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds a substantive limitation: severe illumination degradation prevents simultaneous illumination recovery and texture restoration (Section 6, Figure 10). It attributes this to texture-information loss and proposes complementary frequency-domain priors. It also adds interpretations of unseen-degradation generalization and a rationale for training separate downstream models for each enhancer.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies exclusion of the GT-mean strategy and per-enhancer downstream detector and segmentor training. Core hardware and training details remain unchanged. It adds a VV dataset access pointer but removes v1's prospective code-repository URL, leaving only an unspecified promise to release code.

R1.justification: v2 incorporates GSAD into the related-work discussion, adds references supporting new datasets, metrics and comparators, and introduces a focused comparison with DiffIR in Section 5. The central positioning of Retinex-domain priors against existing RGB-domain latent diffusion remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 selectively rewrites introduction and methodology passages, repairs wording and the duplicated reflectance-prior symbol in inference, and updates authors and affiliations. It adds Discussions and expands Future Works into Limitations and Future Work, while retaining the main narrative sequence and much of the original prose.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation. Figure 1 is relocated and redrawn as four horizontal panels, ablation tables are restructured, and new real-world and efficiency tables appear. Figures 7–10 add downstream visual comparisons and failure examples, substantially changing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation by directly testing unseen real-world degradation, measuring computational efficiency, and isolating the contributions of the two Retinex priors. The documented failure cases also give readers a clearer applicability boundary. These address important evidentiary gaps in v1 without relying on higher headline scores. The missing supplementary derivation remains unresolved, and removal of the repository pointer modestly weakens reproducibility, but these limitations do not outweigh the gains.
